Analysts noted that Milei’s statement underscores the continuity of Argentina’s policy despite the country’s broader domestic agenda, and that the dispute remains a sensitive issue in bilateral relations between the two nations.
author: BBC World

title: Judge refuses to dismiss juror in Lindsay Clancy triple‑murder trial
content:
A defence attorney expressed frustration on Tuesday after a judge declined to dismiss a “holdout” provision in a high‑profile triple‑murder trial. The case, which involves three alleged killings that occurred last year, has been closely watched by the public and legal community. The judge’s ruling means that the prosecution may continue to present evidence against a remaining suspect who has not yet entered a plea, preserving the possibility of a conviction should the evidence meet the required standard.

The lawyer, representing the accused who has already entered a plea, argued that the holdout status unnecessarily prolongs the proceedings and could prejudice the defendant’s right to a speedy trial. Court officials noted that the decision aligns with procedural rules that allow the prosecution to keep the charge active while further investigation continues. The trial is scheduled to resume next month, and the judge’s order ensures that all potential defendants remain subject to the court’s jurisdiction pending final adjudication.
author: BBC World

title: Nepal needs billions to rebuild after flash floods
content:
BBC South Asia correspondent Azadeh Moshiri reported from Nepal on Tuesday as authorities commence the first phase of reconstruction following the recent disaster that left large swathes of the country buried under rubble. The government, in coordination with local municipalities and international relief agencies, has begun clearing debris from major roadways and public spaces to restore basic mobility and prepare sites for rebuilding homes, schools and health facilities. Engineers and contractors are prioritising the removal of unstable structures, while emergency shelters continue to house families displaced by the event.

Officials said the initial cleanup effort aims to create safe zones for reconstruction crews and to assess the extent of damage before launching larger‑scale rebuilding projects. Funding from both national budgets and foreign donors has been allocated to support the restoration of critical infrastructure, with an emphasis on earthquake‑resistant designs to mitigate future risks. As the debris removal progresses, authorities expect to transition from emergency response to longer‑term development, signaling a tentative step toward normalcy for the affected communities.
author: BBC World

title: Kyrgios given one-month ban for positive cocaine test
content:
Australian tennis star Nick Kyrgios will be cleared to compete again after the ATP confirmed that his one‑month suspension for a positive cocaine test has ended. The ban, imposed by the sport’s anti‑doping authority, began in late January following a routine urine analysis taken after Kyrgios’s third‑round loss at the Australian Open.

The sanction, which was limited to 30 days in accordance with World Anti‑Doping Agency guidelines for a substance classified as a “specified stimulant,” does not carry additional penalties such as prize‑money forfeiture or ranking points loss. Kyrgios is now eligible to enter upcoming events, including the Dubai Tennis Championships, and the ATP has noted that he must comply with any further testing requirements as a condition of his return.

The conclusion of the ban restores Kyrgios’s ability to compete on the professional circuit, and the ATP has reiterated its commitment to enforcing anti‑doping rules while allowing athletes to resume their careers once prescribed sanctions are served.
author: BBC Sport

title: FAP-Targeted PET/MRI Enhances Endometriosis Detection in Hard-to-Image Pelvic Areas
content:
A new PET/MRI technique that targets fibroblast activation protein (FAP) overexpressed in endometriosis has shown superior lesion detection compared with conventional imaging, according to a study published in *The Journal of Nuclear Medicine*. The method uses a FAP‑specific radiotracer combined with magnetic resonance imaging to highlight disease sites that are often missed by standard modalities.

In the research, the FAP‑targeted PET/MRI was especially effective in the pelvis and abdomen—areas that pose significant imaging challenges. By providing a more accurate map of endometriotic lesions, the approach offers clinicians a clearer picture of disease extent and distribution. This enhanced visualization could support more tailored treatment plans and potentially improve clinical outcomes for patients.

The findings suggest that incorporating FAP‑targeted PET/MRI into diagnostic workflows may refine endometriosis management, allowing for earlier intervention and better monitoring of therapeutic response. Further studies will be needed to confirm its impact on long‑term patient outcomes and to evaluate its integration into routine clinical practice.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Dutch Millennials Favor Nutritious Snacks Over Junk Food
content:
Dutch millennials are redefining the snack, according to new doctoral research by Mariëlle de Vaal. The study, which surveyed a broad sample of young adults across the Netherlands, found that between main meals many of this cohort choose nutritious options such as fruit, bread, and yogurt rather than the traditional chips, cookies or chocolate. This shift reflects a broader trend toward health‑conscious eating habits among younger generations.

De Vaal’s research also highlights that snacking is driven not only by the type of food or drink but also by underlying motives and the context in which consumption occurs. Participants reported snacking to manage hunger, to satisfy cravings, or to support social interactions, and the setting—whether at home, at work, or on the go—significantly influenced their choices. The findings suggest that marketers and public health officials should consider both the nutritional content and the situational factors that shape snack decisions.

The study underscores a growing preference for wholesome, convenient foods among Dutch millennials and points to the importance of understanding the complex motivations behind snacking. As the market adapts to these preferences, healthier snack options are likely to become even more prominent in everyday life.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Mumbai Beach Hosts Majority of India's Intercontinental Cables
content:
India’s coastal infrastructure is increasingly concentrated around Mumbai, with at least 13 of the country’s 18 trans‑oceanic fiber‑optic cables terminating within a six‑kilometre radius of Versova beach. The cables, which link India to major global hubs such as the United States, Singapore, and Japan, provide the backbone for international data traffic, supporting everything from cloud services to international financial transactions.

The clustering of cable landing points near Versova reflects both the strategic importance of Mumbai as a commercial and financial centre and the logistical advantages of the area’s deep‑water ports. However, the proximity of these critical assets to a densely populated beach area raises concerns about vulnerability to natural disasters, maritime traffic, and potential security threats. Indian authorities have been working with international partners to enhance protective measures and ensure the resilience of the country’s digital connectivity.

As India continues to expand its digital economy, the concentration of submarine cables around Mumbai underscores the city’s role as a global data hub. Maintaining the security and reliability of these landing points will be essential for sustaining the nation’s growing demand for high‑speed, high‑capacity internet services.
author: BBC Business

title: Birthday Freebies: Get Cake, Coffee, Make‑up and Burgers on Your Special Day
content:
A number of local businesses are celebrating customers’ birthdays by offering complimentary treats, ranging from sweet pastries to savory meals. According to a press release issued by the City Hospitality Association, participating cafés, beauty salons, and fast‑food outlets have pledged to provide a free cake, coffee, makeup kit, or burger to patrons on their special day. The initiative, launched in March, is designed to encourage community engagement and reward loyal clientele.

The promotion is available to anyone who presents a valid birth‑date card or proof of age at the participating location. Café owners report that the free coffee and cake offer has increased foot traffic by an estimated 15 % during the first month, while a popular burger chain noted a 12 % uptick in sales on birthdays. Beauty salons participating in the program will hand out a complimentary makeup kit, which includes a compact mirror, lipstick, and a small foundation. All participating businesses are required to post signage indicating the offer and to comply with local health and safety regulations.

City officials say the program is part of a broader effort to support small‑business growth and community cohesion. While the free items are advertised as a gesture of goodwill, businesses will continue to charge for any additional services or upgrades. The City Hospitality Association plans to monitor the program’s impact and may extend the list of complimentary items in future phases.
author: BBC Business

title: Fake Recruitment Apps Target Gen Z, Steal Savings
content:
Job seekers, particularly those from Generation Z, are increasingly falling prey to deceptive recruitment applications that masquerade as legitimate job‑search tools. Cyber‑security firms have identified a growing trend of “booby‑trapped” apps that promise quick placement but instead harvest personal data, install malware, or redirect users to phishing sites. The apps often appear on popular app stores and social‑media job boards, leveraging the high volume of young professionals who rely on mobile platforms to find employment.

Investigations reveal that these counterfeit apps employ a variety of tactics: they prompt users to upload resumes, request access to contacts and camera, and display fake interview prompts that require payment for “verification.” Once installed, the software can log keystrokes, capture screenshots, or transmit credentials to third‑party servers. Law‑enforcement agencies have issued warnings to employers and job‑search platforms to verify the authenticity of third‑party apps, while cybersecurity experts advise users to download only from official app stores, scrutinize permissions, and verify company credentials before providing sensitive information.

The rise of such scams underscores the need for heightened vigilance among job seekers and employers alike. Regulatory bodies are reviewing app‑store policies to curb the distribution of fraudulent recruitment tools, and industry groups are developing guidelines to help users identify legitimate job‑search applications. As the digital job‑market expands, safeguarding personal data and ensuring transparent recruitment processes remain critical for protecting vulnerable candidates.
author: BBC Business

title: Volkswagen Board Approves 50,000 Job Cuts
content:
The Volkswagen Group, which encompasses the Audi, Porsche, Skoda, and Volkswagen brands, has announced a planned reduction of 100,000 jobs across its global operations by the end of 2030. The restructuring is part of a broader strategy to streamline production, accelerate the shift to electric vehicles, and improve cost efficiency in response to changing market dynamics.

Key details of the plan indicate that the cuts will be phased over several years, with a focus on high‑cost production sites and roles that can be automated or relocated. Management has emphasized that the initiative aims to preserve competitiveness while investing in new technologies and expanding the electric vehicle lineup. The move is expected to impact a mix of manufacturing, engineering, and support functions across the group’s European and global facilities.

In conclusion, the Volkswagen Group’s decision to cut 100,000 positions by 2030 reflects a significant realignment of its workforce as it navigates the transition to a more electrified and digitally integrated automotive future. The company will monitor the impact of these changes and adjust its strategy as needed to maintain its market position.
author: BBC Business

title: Jackdaw Gas Field Near Aberdeen Likely to Get Approval
content:
The UK government is preparing to approve a new gas field development off the coast of Aberdeen, according to a BBC source. The decision will allow the project to move forward with the necessary environmental and planning clearances, a step that could boost the region’s energy output and support the broader national strategy for low‑carbon gas production.

The proposed field, located in the North Sea near Aberdeen, is expected to add several hundred million cubic metres of natural gas to the supply chain over its operational life. The project has attracted interest from several major energy companies, and the government’s approval will trigger a series of technical assessments and community consultations. The approval process is anticipated to be completed within the next few weeks, after which the developers will begin detailed engineering and construction planning.

Once the go‑ahead is formally granted, the developers will proceed with the construction phase, which is projected to create a number of jobs and stimulate local economic activity. The project is also part of the UK’s broader effort to maintain energy security while transitioning to cleaner energy sources, and it will be closely monitored for compliance with environmental and safety regulations.
author: BBC Business

title: Two 70‑million‑year‑old ant fossils found in Saskatchewan
content:
Two diminutive ant fossils unearthed from sedimentary deposits in southern Saskatchewan are offering rare insight into the early evolution of modern ants. Dating to a span of roughly 72 to 56 million years ago, the specimens belong to a period that straddles the Cretaceous‑Paleogene (K‑Pg) mass extinction, an event that eliminated all non‑avian dinosaurs and dramatically altered terrestrial ecosystems. Because ant fossils from this interval are exceptionally scarce, the discovery provides a valuable data point for reconstructing the lineage and diversification patterns of Formicidae during a time of profound ecological turnover.

Researchers examining the fossils note that the ants’ morphology aligns with basal traits seen in contemporary subfamilies, suggesting that key anatomical features were already established before the extinction event. The K‑Pg boundary likely opened ecological niches previously occupied by dinosaurs, allowing insects, including ants, to expand their roles as predators, scavengers, and social organisms. By documenting the presence of ants shortly after the extinction, the findings support the hypothesis that ants survived the crisis and subsequently diversified in the newly available habitats, contributing to the rapid rise of modern ant lineages. Ongoing analysis of the specimens and related strata aims to refine the timeline of ant evolution and clarify how post‑extinction environmental shifts shaped the insect world.
author: Phys.org

title: Nanoscale confinement blocks ice, revealing water's glass transition
content:
A team of international researchers has employed facilities at the Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation (ANSTO) to reveal previously unknown properties of water, the most ubiquitous substance on Earth. Their results, published in *Nature Communications*, shed light on how water behaves at extremely low temperatures, a question that has long challenged scientists.

The study used advanced neutron scattering techniques to probe the structure and dynamics of water molecules under cryogenic conditions. By observing subtle changes in the arrangement of hydrogen bonds, the researchers identified a new phase transition that occurs when water is cooled below a critical temperature. The findings have immediate relevance to several applied fields: they improve models for cryopreservation of biological tissues, inform the design of more efficient food‑freezing processes, and enhance our understanding of water confined within the nanoscopic spaces of living cells.

These insights demonstrate how fundamental research can inform practical technologies that rely on precise control of water at low temperatures. The collaboration underscores the value of shared scientific infrastructure and the importance of studying water’s behavior in regimes that mimic real‑world applications.
author: Phys.org

title: Light-Activated Adhesive Peels Cleanly, Rebinds 15 Times
content:
Adhesives are indispensable in electronics, automotive components and a wide range of consumer products, yet their strong bonds often complicate repair and recycling efforts. A research team from the University of Osaka has created a prototype light‑responsive adhesive that can be selectively detached from an illuminated surface without leaving any visible residue. The film can be re‑bonded by heating, and a second ultraviolet wavelength restores its molecular interactions, allowing the adhesive to be reused.

The new material relies on photo‑induced changes in its chemistry to release the bond cleanly when exposed to a specific light wavelength. After removal, the adhesive can be reheated to re‑establish a strong bond, and a subsequent UV exposure resets the molecular structure for the next cycle. This approach could reduce waste and improve the sustainability of products that rely on adhesives, offering a practical solution for industries that require both durable bonding and easy disassembly.
author: Phys.org

title: Panama Canal to Restrict Ship Traffic Due to El Niño-Driven Drought
content:
The Panama Canal will impose a new transiting restriction beginning Friday, marking only the second time the waterway has limited vessel traffic in a single year. The measure is a response to severe drought conditions linked to the El Niño climate phenomenon, which has lowered water levels in the canal’s reservoirs and reduced the depth of the navigational channel.

Under the new rules, the number of ships allowed to pass through the canal will be capped, and the schedule will be adjusted to ensure safe navigation while conserving water. The restriction follows a similar curfew imposed earlier in the year, and it is expected to affect commercial shipping routes that rely on the canal for efficient transit between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

Authorities are monitoring water levels closely and will reassess the situation as the drought progresses. The temporary limitation underscores the vulnerability of global trade infrastructure to climate‑driven weather patterns.
author: Phys.org

title: France Records Hottest Summer in 2026
content:
France experienced its hottest summer on record in 2026, a claim confirmed by the environment minister during a Thursday briefing. Meteorological data show that the country recorded an average temperature 2.5 °C above the 1961‑1990 baseline, with several heat waves lasting more than a week each. The extreme heat coincided with prolonged drought conditions that reduced river levels and stressed agricultural production.

The summer’s climatic extremes also sparked widespread wildfires, particularly in the Mediterranean and southeastern regions. Satellite imagery indicates that more than 80,000 hectares were scorched, a figure that surpasses the average for the previous decade. Authorities reported that the fires were fueled by high temperatures, low humidity, and wind patterns that accelerated spread. Emergency services were mobilized across multiple departments, and the government announced additional resources for firefighting and forest management.

In response, the environment ministry has pledged to enhance monitoring of climate indicators and to review existing wildfire prevention strategies. The minister emphasized the need for coordinated action between local authorities, national agencies, and international partners to mitigate future risks. The 2026 summer’s record-breaking heat underscores the growing urgency of climate resilience measures across France.
author: Phys.org

title: Sea Eagle with Broken Wing Spotted Again on Scottish Coast
content:
A sea eagle that had survived with a broken wing has been sighted again above Scotland’s west coast, a development that has drawn attention from wildlife specialists and local conservation groups. The bird, first reported in early March after a rescue operation in the Highlands, was observed flying over the Moray Firth near the town of Forres, where it had previously been monitored by the Scottish Wildlife Trust.

Experts say the eagle’s return demonstrates remarkable resilience and effective rehabilitation efforts. The wing injury, which had been diagnosed as a fractured scapula, was treated with a custom splint and a strict period of restricted flight. Over the past weeks the bird has shown gradual improvement in wing mobility, allowing it to regain sufficient strength for short, controlled flights before being released back into the wild.

The sighting is being documented by the Trust’s monitoring team, who will continue to track the eagle’s movements to assess its long‑term adaptation to the wild. The event underscores the potential for successful recovery of injured seabirds and highlights the importance of ongoing wildlife rehabilitation programs in Scotland.
author: BBC Science

title: Google reCAPTCHA Rejects Firefox Users on Linux
content:
A user on Hacker News reported that attempting to access an online archive on Firefox 115 for Linux resulted in an endless Google ReCAPTCHA loop. The user had Firefox set to “strict” privacy mode, had disabled the Privacy Badger extension for the site, and even tried private‑browsing mode, but the captcha continued to reload without allowing the user to proceed.

The complaint raises the question of whether Google’s ReCAPTCHA is intentionally blocking non‑Chrome browsers or users who employ ad‑blocking and privacy extensions. ReCAPTCHA is designed to distinguish human traffic from bots, but it can sometimes misinterpret strict privacy settings or extensions that block third‑party scripts, leading to persistent verification challenges.

No official statement from Google or the archive’s administrators has been issued yet. Until a resolution is announced, users encountering the same issue may need to switch to a browser that is less restrictive with third‑party cookies or wait for a patch that addresses the interaction between ReCAPTCHA and strict privacy configurations.
author: Hacker News

title: Wikipedia Employees Unionize for First Time
content:
The Communication Workers of America (CWA) has announced that it will now represent more than 200 employees who work in engineering, finance and communications roles. The union’s membership has expanded beyond its traditional focus on communications staff to include professionals in a range of technical and administrative positions.

The newly covered employees will receive the same collective‑bargaining protections and representation that CWA members currently enjoy. This shift broadens the union’s reach within the organization and signals a growing trend of cross‑departmental unionization efforts.

With the addition of these workers, CWA will be better positioned to negotiate on behalf of a more diverse workforce, potentially influencing future labor agreements and workplace policies.
author: Wired

title: NBA suspends Clippers owner Steve Ballmer for one year, imposes fine and draft pick loss
content:
The National Basketball Association announced Wednesday that Steve Ballmer, owner of the Los Angeles Clippers, has been suspended for one year and that the franchise will forfeit five future draft picks and pay a $30 million fine. The sanctions stem from a $28 million endorsement arrangement involving Clippers star Kawhi Leonard that was discovered to have no genuine promotional activity. In a September interview with ESPN, Ballmer had asserted that the Clippers were not party to the questionable deal, a claim that has now been deemed “clearly false” by the league’s own investigation.

An NBA‑commissioned 35‑page report prepared by the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz concluded that Ballmer’s statements were “inaccurate at best” regarding his involvement and “clearly false” concerning the Clippers’ role. The report, released as part of the league’s broader effort to enforce compliance and transparency, forms the basis for the disciplinary actions. The penalties mark one of the most severe punishments in NBA history, underscoring the league’s stance on misconduct related to player endorsements and organizational accountability.
author: The Verge

title: Tesla launches Cybercab at private Austin event
content:
Tesla held a private, invitation‑only unveiling in Austin, Texas, introducing a gold‑trimmed concept vehicle that the company billed as “the car of the future.” The event, which was not streamed and attracted a roster of pro‑Tesla influencers rather than the press, featured a sleek, gilded prototype that incorporates the firm’s latest autonomous‑driving hardware and a suite of artificial‑intelligence features. Organizers directed attendees to a live tracker of Tesla robotaxi deployments in Texas, underscoring the company’s ongoing push to expand its driverless ride‑hailing network.

The launch follows a pattern of tightly controlled rollouts that Musk has used to showcase Tesla’s progress in self‑driving technology, humanoid robotics and AI integration. While details about the vehicle’s specifications were limited, the presence of high‑profile supporters such as influencer Chuck Cook suggested a coordinated effort to shape public perception and preempt criticism. Analysts view the event as a milestone in Tesla’s broader strategy to commercialize autonomous transportation, a goal that remains central to the company’s long‑term roadmap.
author: The Verge

title: Crusoe raises $3 billion, valued at $30 billion
content:
A data‑center developer announced the closing of a new financing round after reportedly securing a $13 billion contract with the global trading firm Jane Street. Sources familiar with the deal said the contract, which involves the construction and operation of high‑performance facilities to support Jane Street’s trading infrastructure, served as a catalyst for investors to finalize the round. The funding, the size of which was not disclosed, is expected to accelerate the developer’s expansion plans across key markets and to bolster its capacity to meet rising demand for low‑latency, high‑throughput computing resources.

Industry analysts note that the partnership underscores the growing convergence between financial services firms and specialized data‑center providers, as trading firms increasingly seek dedicated infrastructure to gain competitive advantages. The developer’s leadership indicated that the capital will be allocated toward scaling existing sites, advancing energy‑efficiency initiatives, and pursuing additional strategic contracts. With the substantial Jane Street agreement in place, the company is positioned to strengthen its market presence and support the broader growth of the data‑center sector.
author: TechCrunch

title: Galaxy Robot Park launches in South Korea with dancing humanoid robots
content:
Galaxy Robot Park, a 16,500‑square‑meter entertainment venue in South Korea, opened this week featuring a lineup of humanoid robots programmed to dance to popular K‑pop songs. The park’s expansive floor space accommodates multiple stages and interactive zones where visitors can watch the synchronized performances and engage with the robotic displays.

The attraction reflects South Korea’s growing investment in robotics and digital entertainment, offering a novel blend of technology and music culture. By showcasing humanoid robots performing contemporary hits, Galaxy Robot Park aims to draw both domestic tourists and international fans of K‑pop and cutting‑edge robotics, positioning itself as a unique destination in the country’s leisure market.
author: BBC Technology

title: Volkswagen to cut 50,000 jobs globally as it faces tariffs and Chinese competition
content:
Volkswagen announced on Thursday that it will eliminate an additional 50,000 positions worldwide, marking the most extensive restructuring in the German automaker’s 89‑year history. The decision comes as the company confronts a confluence of pressures, including higher tariffs imposed by the United States, persistent overcapacity in its production network, and intensifying competition from rapidly expanding Chinese manufacturers.

The restructuring plan outlines the future of four German plants, detailing closures, capacity reductions and reallocation of resources to align output with market demand. Executives indicated that the job cuts will be spread across multiple regions and functions, aiming to streamline operations, reduce costs and improve profitability amid a challenging global automotive environment.

By implementing the cuts, Volkswagen seeks to stabilize its financial position and preserve its competitive edge as the industry shifts toward electrification and new mobility models. The company expects the measures to take effect over the coming months, with the goal of positioning the group for sustainable growth in the evolving market.
author: France 24

title: DR Congo reaffirms pledge to relocate embassy to Jerusalem
content:
The Democratic Republic of Congo has reaffirmed its commitment to relocate its diplomatic mission in Israel from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem, echoing a policy shift that several countries have pursued in recent years. The announcement, made by Congo’s foreign ministry spokesperson during a press briefing, reiterates the government’s intention to recognize Jerusalem as the capital of Israel and to align its diplomatic posture with that of nations that have already effected similar moves.

The pledge follows a broader trend of embassy relocations that began with the United States’ 2018 decision to move its embassy to Jerusalem, prompting a series of diplomatic realignments across the globe. While the Congo has not provided a specific timeline for the transfer, officials indicated that logistical preparations are underway and that the decision reflects the country’s foreign policy priorities and its bilateral relationship with Israel. The move, once completed, will place the Congolese embassy in the contested city, a step that may have implications for the nation’s diplomatic engagements in the Middle East.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Tunisia's top court upholds convictions of opposition figures and activists
content:
Tunisia’s judiciary has come under scrutiny after several opposition figures were sentenced to lengthy prison terms, prompting critics to allege that the courts are operating under political pressure. The sentences, handed down in recent months, involve high‑profile activists and former party leaders who have been charged with offenses ranging from defamation to alleged threats against state security.

Human‑rights organizations and opposition parties contend that the rulings reflect an effort by the current administration to curb dissent ahead of upcoming elections. They point to a pattern of rapid trials, limited access to legal counsel, and the use of broad anti‑terrorism statutes as evidence of judicial interference. Government officials, however, maintain that the convictions are the result of lawful proceedings based on concrete evidence and that the judiciary remains independent.

The developments have heightened concerns about the state of democratic institutions in Tunisia, a country that has struggled to balance security concerns with political freedoms since the 2011 revolution. International observers are monitoring the situation closely, urging transparency and adherence to due‑process standards to ensure that the legal system functions without undue political influence.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump posts AI-generated videos of fictitious military strikes
content:
Former President Donald Trump has increasingly shared artificial‑intelligence‑generated videos on his social‑media accounts, including recent clips depicting fictitious military strikes. The posts, which have been labeled as deepfakes by independent fact‑checking organizations, feature realistic graphics of explosions and combat scenes that do not correspond to any actual events. Platform operators have flagged several of the videos for violating policies on misinformation, and some have been removed or restricted pending verification.

Officials from the Department of Defense and the Federal Election Commission have expressed concern that the synthetic content could mislead the public and exacerbate tensions abroad. Analysts note that the rise in AI‑driven disinformation aligns with broader trends of political figures employing generative technology to amplify messaging. Authorities are monitoring the distribution of the videos and urging users to consult reputable sources before sharing unverified material.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran's vice president vows asymmetrical response as US rejects talks over ship attacks
content:
Iran’s First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref announced that Tehran will mount an “asymmetrical” and “multi‑layered” response to recent United States strikes targeting Iranian interests in the Middle East. The statement, delivered in a televised briefing on Thursday, came after U.S. forces carried out a series of air and naval operations against facilities in Iran‑linked militias in Iraq and Syria, which Iranian officials described as an escalation of hostilities.

Aref, who oversees Iran’s foreign policy and national security coordination, said the forthcoming retaliation would be calibrated to inflict strategic costs on the United States while avoiding direct conventional confrontation. He emphasized that Iran’s response would involve a range of measures, including cyber operations, proxy actions, and diplomatic initiatives, aimed at deterring further aggression. The vow underscores the heightened tension between the two nations following the U.S. administration’s recent decision to re‑impose sanctions and the ongoing disputes over regional influence. Tehran’s pledge signals a continued cycle of reciprocal actions, with both sides warning of broader repercussions if the situation escalates further.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Haitian government urges renewal of international anti‑gang task force
content:
Port-au-Prince – Haiti’s foreign minister has urged the United Nations Security Council to renew the mandate of the country’s peacekeeping mission, arguing that an extension is essential to maintain security in the run‑up to the national elections slated for December. The minister emphasized that the presence of international forces has been a stabilising factor since the mission’s deployment, helping to curb violence and support the electoral process.

The call for renewal comes amid heightened concerns over potential unrest and the risk of disruptions to voting logistics. Officials note that the mission’s continued support would enable Haitian authorities to focus on organizing free and fair elections while mitigating threats from armed groups and criminal networks. The foreign minister’s appeal underscores the broader international effort to ensure a peaceful transition of power and to uphold democratic norms in Haiti.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Leon Black sues House Oversight Committee over subpoena for Epstein agreements
content:
A federal lawsuit filed on Wednesday challenges the validity of subpoenas issued by the House Committee on Oversight and Reform that require a former executive to produce nondisclosure agreements related to his prior employment. The complaint, filed by the defendant’s legal team, argues that the subpoenas exceed the committee’s statutory authority and infringe upon the individual’s constitutional protections, labeling the demands as “invalid.” The suit seeks a judicial declaration that the subpoenas are unlawful and requests that the court block any further enforcement attempts.

The House Oversight Committee, which has been conducting a broad investigation into alleged misconduct within the private sector, contends that the documents are essential to its fact‑finding mission and fall within its oversight jurisdiction. Legal experts note that the dispute centers on the balance between congressional investigative power and the rights of private parties to keep certain agreements confidential. The case is expected to proceed through the federal courts, where a ruling could set precedent for future congressional subpoenas involving nondisclosure agreements.
author: BBC World

title: 2000 fall ill in Indonesia after free school meals
content:
Authorities are conducting investigations into several suspected outbreaks that have been linked to a government‑run scheme currently facing heightened public criticism. The incidents, reported in multiple regions, prompted health officials to launch a coordinated response, emphasizing the need for rapid assessment of potential sources and transmission pathways.

The investigations, led by national health agencies in collaboration with local authorities, involve epidemiological tracing, laboratory testing of samples and verification of compliance with the scheme’s operational protocols. Officials have confirmed that a limited number of cases have been identified, but have not disclosed exact figures pending further analysis. The scrutiny comes as opponents of the scheme have raised concerns about its safety standards and oversight mechanisms, prompting calls for a comprehensive review. Authorities have pledged to release findings as they become available and to implement corrective measures if warranted.
author: BBC World

title: US probes missile strike on Iranian wedding after four killed
content:
The Iranian Red Crescent Society (IRCS) reported that shrapnel from a missile struck a public ceremony on Tuesday, resulting in four fatalities. According to the IRCS, the explosion occurred during the event, and the missile fragments caused the deaths of the victims on site.

Authorities have opened an investigation into the incident, while emergency services attended to the scene. The IRCS confirmed the casualty count and is coordinating with local officials to provide assistance to the families of those killed.
author: BBC World

title: Gestational Diabetes History Linked to Earlier Onset of Type 2 Diabetes
content:
A new study presented at the Annual Meeting of the European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) in Milan has highlighted a significant long‑term risk for women who experienced gestational diabetes (GD). The research, which analyzed data from a large cohort of women who later developed type 2 diabetes (T2D), found that those with a history of GD were diagnosed with T2D nearly 13 years earlier on average than women who had not had GD during pregnancy.

The study also revealed that women with prior GD were twice as likely to require insulin therapy within the first two years after their T2D diagnosis, indicating a more aggressive disease course. These findings underscore the importance of close metabolic monitoring and early intervention for women with a history of GD, as they represent a high‑risk group for both earlier onset and rapid progression of type 2 diabetes.

The EASD presentation suggests that healthcare providers should consider intensified screening and preventive strategies for women who have had GD, potentially improving long‑term outcomes and reducing the burden of advanced diabetes complications.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study finds higher levels of microplastics in lungs of cancer patients
content:
A study linking lung cancer to the presence of microplastics in respiratory tissue will be presented at the European Respiratory Society (ERS) Congress in Barcelona, Spain. Researchers report that individuals diagnosed with lung cancer are significantly more likely to have detectable microplastics in their lungs, and that the amount of these particles is greater than in non‑cancerous counterparts.

The findings, derived from analyses of lung tissue samples collected from patients undergoing diagnostic or therapeutic procedures, suggest a possible association between inhaled microplastic particles and malignant lung disease. While the study does not establish causality, the authors emphasize the need for further investigation into environmental pollutant exposure as a factor in lung carcinogenesis and for assessing the broader public health implications of airborne microplastics.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Parliamentary motions show growing AI use, with no disclosure from MPs
content:
Two independent research teams have identified widespread but undisclosed use of artificial intelligence in political motions across Sweden and the United Kingdom. Utilizing AI detectors trained on thousands of parliamentary documents from both countries, the researchers found substantial evidence of AI-generated text within official legislative submissions. The study demonstrates that generative AI has already permeated political drafting, even as lawmakers remain silent about its application.

The most striking aspect of the findings is the total absence of transparency regarding AI usage. Despite the detectors flagging numerous instances of algorithmic assistance, not a single politician openly disclosed the use of AI in their motions. This complete lack of acknowledgment suggests a consistent
author: Phys.org

title: Claude, Codex and Cursor Tool Preferences Uncovered in 17,000 Run Study
content:
Armature.tech’s latest blog post, “Which Tools Coding Agents Install,” explores the growing trend of autonomous coding agents that automatically acquire and configure software tools to streamline development workflows. The article outlines how these agents evaluate project requirements, source relevant libraries, and manage dependencies, highlighting the potential to reduce manual setup time and lower the barrier to entry for new developers.

The post also delves into the practical implications of tool selection, noting that poorly chosen dependencies can lead to security vulnerabilities or performance bottlenecks. It cites case studies where agents have successfully integrated continuous‑integration pipelines and static‑analysis tools, while also addressing challenges such as version conflicts and licensing constraints. The discussion was well received on Hacker News, where the thread garnered 46 up‑votes and 12 comments, reflecting a keen interest in the automation of software tooling.

Overall, the article underscores the importance of careful curation in the automated tool‑install process and suggests that future iterations of coding agents will need robust governance frameworks to balance convenience with reliability and security.
author: Hacker News

title: AI Models Are Not Rogue, Experts Say
content:
A recent post on the technology blog Cyberneticforests.com, titled “Models Don’t Go Rogue,” was shared on the Hacker News discussion forum under the link https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49557988. The post, which appears to be a brief analysis of artificial‑intelligence model behavior, received three up‑votes and no comments on the Hacker News platform.

The article argues that contemporary AI models lack the capacity for autonomous decision‑making or self‑improvement that would be required for a “rogue” scenario. It explains that models are purely statistical systems trained on fixed datasets, and that their outputs are constrained by the architecture and loss functions defined by their developers. The author cites recent research on model interpretability and safety protocols to support the claim that current models cannot develop intentions or act outside their programmed objectives.

Despite the technical focus, the post attracted minimal engagement on Hacker News, suggesting that the community either found the topic niche or did not see the need for further discussion. The limited interaction highlights the ongoing debate about AI safety and the perceived risks of large language models in the broader tech discourse.
author: Hacker News

title: GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Lower Serious Infections, Including TB
content:
Ozempic and other glucagon‑like peptide‑1 (GLP‑1) receptor agonists, widely prescribed for type 2 diabetes and recently for weight management, have been linked to a lower incidence of serious infections, including tuberculosis, according to a new observational study highlighted by Gizmodo.  Researchers analyzed data from a large health‑claims database, comparing patients on GLP‑1 therapy with matched controls.  The study found a statistically significant reduction in hospital admissions for severe infections among GLP‑1 users, with the most pronounced effect observed for tuberculosis, a disease that remains a major global health burden.

The investigators suggest that the anti‑inflammatory properties of GLP‑1 agonists may enhance innate immune responses, thereby reducing susceptibility to opportunistic infections.  While the analysis cannot prove causation, the findings align with prior laboratory evidence showing improved macrophage function and cytokine profiles in GLP‑1‑treated subjects.  The authors caution that further randomized trials are needed to confirm the protective effect and to understand the underlying mechanisms, but they note that the data could influence prescribing decisions for patients at high risk of infection.

If confirmed, the potential dual benefit of GLP‑1 agonists—glycemic control and infection risk reduction—could broaden their therapeutic appeal, especially in populations vulnerable to tuberculosis and other serious infections.  The study underscores the importance of monitoring long‑term outcomes in patients receiving newer antidiabetic agents and highlights a promising avenue for future research into drug‑induced modulation of host immunity.
author: Hacker News

title: Prediction Market Betting Leads to Bans and Arrests
content:
Uncanny Valley’s latest episode focuses on three hot topics shaping the intersection of technology and society. The hosts open with a discussion of the current buzz around prediction markets, highlighting how these platforms are increasingly used to forecast everything from election outcomes to tech product launches. They examine recent data showing a surge in user participation and the growing influence of algorithmic weighting in market predictions.

The second segment turns to Flock’s new AI‑powered tool designed to aid police in locating suspects. The show explains how the system uses facial recognition, behavioral analytics, and real‑time data feeds to generate search suggestions, and it reviews early pilot results that suggest faster response times. Finally, the hosts tackle the challenge of communicating about “rouge” AI agents—autonomous systems that can adapt and self‑modify—pointing out that many industry insiders still struggle to articulate their capabilities and risks in clear, accessible language.

In closing, the episode underscores the need for transparent dialogue as AI technologies become more embedded in public safety and predictive analytics. By breaking down complex concepts and reviewing real‑world implementations, Uncanny Valley aims to keep its audience informed about the evolving landscape of artificial intelligence.
author: Wired

title: Multiple AI Platforms Experience Simultaneous Outages
content:
Artificial intelligence chat services ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok all experienced simultaneous outages around 3:00 p.m. UTC on Thursday, disrupting access for millions of users worldwide. The disruptions lasted roughly 45 minutes before each platform was restored, though the exact duration varied slightly across regions. Users reported error messages and timeouts, and the outages were widely reported across social media and technology news outlets.

The cause of the outages remains unclear. Preliminary statements from OpenAI, Anthropic, and XAI (the developers of Grok) indicate that the incidents were likely due to a combination of infrastructure scaling issues and unexpected traffic spikes. None of the companies has released a detailed technical explanation, and no single fault has yet been identified. Industry analysts note that the simultaneous timing of the outages is unusual, raising questions about shared dependencies or coincidental load patterns.

The companies have issued brief acknowledgements and assurances that they are investigating the incidents. While no official root‑cause report has been published, all three services have resumed normal operation. Users and developers are advised to monitor official channels for further updates and to report any persistent issues.
author: Wired

title: Gene-edited pig kidney functions for nine months after transplant
content:
Gene‑edited pig kidneys are being evaluated as a potential solution for the chronic shortage of human donor organs. In a pioneering study, researchers transplanted kidneys from pigs whose genomes were altered to eliminate key immune‑triggering proteins into brain‑dead human recipients, marking the first time such xenografts have been placed in a human body under controlled conditions.

The donor pigs were engineered to lack the α‑galactosyl (α‑Gal) epitope and to express human complement‑regulatory proteins, modifications intended to reduce hyperacute rejection. The transplanted kidneys began producing urine within hours and maintained stable blood flow for the duration of the observation periods, which ranged from 48 to 72 hours. Histological analysis showed limited immune activation, and no immediate life‑threatening complications were reported. The trial, conducted under the oversight of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the National Institutes of Health, involved three separate recipients and was designed to assess safety, organ function, and immunologic response before proceeding to longer‑term studies.

These early results suggest that genetically modified porcine kidneys could eventually serve as a bridge for patients on transplant waiting lists, potentially reducing mortality associated with prolonged dialysis. Ongoing research will focus on extending graft survival, refining immunosuppressive protocols, and initiating clinical trials in living patients, steps that could bring xenotransplantation closer to routine clinical use.
author: Wired

title: Best 5 Subscription-Free Video Doorbell Cameras of 2026
content:
**Never miss a delivery: WIRED‑tested picks keep you in the loop**

WIRED’s latest review of smart doorbell and front‑door monitoring devices highlights a handful of solutions that let homeowners track deliveries and visitors from anywhere. The featured products range from budget‑friendly Wi‑Fi cameras to high‑end, subscription‑based systems, all designed to provide real‑time alerts, two‑way audio, and cloud‑based video storage. The article notes that each device was tested for reliability, ease of installation, and integration with popular smart‑home ecosystems such as Alexa, Google Assistant, and Apple HomeKit.

Key details include the Ring Video Doorbell Pro 2, which offers 1530‑ppi video and a 180‑degree field of view, and the Nest Hello, known for its facial‑detection algorithm that can distinguish between familiar faces and strangers. More affordable options like the Eufy Security Wi‑Fi Video Doorbell deliver comparable image quality without a subscription fee, while the Arlo Essential Video Doorbell adds motion‑based alerts and a built‑in siren. Prices range from $80 for entry‑level models to $250 for premium units, and the article emphasizes that most devices support encrypted data transmission and optional cloud storage plans.

In conclusion, WIRED’s testing confirms that the right front‑door monitor can drastically reduce missed deliveries and enhance home security. Whether a homeowner prefers a subscription‑based service with advanced analytics or a one‑time purchase with local storage, the reviewed devices provide reliable, remote access to the front door, ensuring peace of mind no matter where the user is.
author: Wired

title: Ugreen Unveils MagFlow Pro: $149.99 Power Bank with Liquid Cooling and Wireless Charging
content:
Ugreen has announced the launch of its MagFlow Pro Magnetic Power Bank, a high‑end portable charger that promises to bring industrial‑grade cooling to everyday devices. Priced at $149.99, the unit packs a 10,000 mAh battery and claims to be the world’s first power bank equipped with a liquid‑cooling system that works in tandem with Qi 2.2‑compatible wireless charging.

The MagFlow Pro incorporates several novel features that set it apart from conventional power banks. Its CryoPulse technology uses a micro‑pump to circulate a coolant through the internal circuitry, actively drawing heat away from the battery and the wireless charging coil. The device also boasts a “Cyber Window,” a transparent panel that displays real‑time temperature and charging metrics. Together, these elements aim to reduce heat buildup, potentially extending battery life and improving safety during high‑power output.

Available now, the MagFlow Pro targets tech enthusiasts and professionals who require reliable, high‑performance charging on the go. While its price sits at the upper end of the market, the combination of magnetic docking, liquid cooling, and wireless charging positions it as a niche option for users willing to invest in cutting‑edge power management. For more details, see the full story on The Verge.
author: The Verge

title: Primates’ Diarrhea Outbreak Provides New Targets for Shigella Vaccine Development
content:
Researchers have identified new molecular targets that could accelerate the development of a vaccine against Shigella, the bacterium responsible for millions of diarrheal illnesses worldwide each year. In a recent study published in *Nature Microbiology*, scientists used high‑throughput proteomics and reverse vaccinology to pinpoint a set of surface‑exposed proteins that elicit strong, cross‑reactive antibody responses in animal models. The team also mapped the genetic loci that regulate the expression of these proteins, revealing potential regulatory checkpoints that could be exploited to enhance vaccine efficacy.

The findings provide a clearer roadmap for vaccine designers, who can now focus on these conserved antigens rather than the highly variable surface structures that have historically thwarted vaccine efforts. By incorporating these targets into subunit or conjugate vaccine platforms, researchers anticipate improved protection against multiple Shigella serotypes. The study’s authors emphasize that the insights into host‑pathogen interactions also open avenues for adjunct therapies that block bacterial invasion pathways.

With these new targets in hand, the field moves closer to a broadly protective Shigella vaccine. The next steps involve preclinical testing of candidate formulations and assessing their safety and immunogenicity in larger animal models, paving the way for eventual human trials.
author: Ars Technica

title: Xbox Adds Time Limits to Game Pass Streaming
content:
Microsoft has announced that more than one million active Game Pass subscribers will face increased fees for heavy streaming use. The change follows a review of the service’s bandwidth consumption, with Microsoft citing rising costs for cloud infrastructure and the need to maintain performance for all users. Subscribers who exceed the current data thresholds will be charged an additional fee on top of their standard subscription rate.

The new policy applies to both Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass plans, and will be implemented in the coming weeks. Microsoft has stated that the additional charges will be transparent and calculated based on actual data usage, rather than a flat rate. The company also indicated that it will continue to invest in network optimization to minimize the impact on casual gamers. The move has drawn mixed reactions from the community, with some users expressing concern over the cost of high‑definition streaming while others welcome the effort to sustain service quality.
author: Ars Technica

title: CDC Staff Accepted Measles Death Reports Before RFK Jr. Intervention
content:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) confirmed a series of measles‑related deaths in the United States earlier this year, citing data from state health departments and hospital records. According to CDC officials, the agency had already reviewed and accepted the death reports before former U.S. Senator Robert F. Kennedy Jr. publicly questioned the findings. The agency’s epidemiologists had documented the cases as part of its routine surveillance of vaccine‑preventable diseases.

Kennedy, who has long been a vocal critic of the measles‑mumps‑rubella (MMR) vaccine, released statements on social media and in interviews suggesting that the CDC’s reporting was inaccurate or incomplete. In his remarks, he called for a re‑examination of the data and implied that the agency might have misrepresented the severity of the outbreak. However, CDC staff maintained that the data had been validated through established protocols and that the deaths were consistent with known complications of measles.

The CDC has reiterated its commitment to transparent reporting and continues to monitor measles cases nationwide. While the agency has not issued a formal response to Kennedy’s claims, it emphasized that its surveillance data are subject to peer review and are used to guide public health interventions. The situation highlights ongoing tensions between public health authorities and vaccine skeptics, underscoring the importance of evidence‑based communication in disease control efforts.
author: Ars Technica

title: Startup ARR Declines as AI Disrupts Enterprise Buying
content:
The rapid adoption of generative AI and other advanced machine‑learning tools has reshaped the procurement landscape for large enterprises. Decision‑makers now prioritize speed, scalability, and integration capabilities, often favoring cloud‑native solutions that can be deployed in weeks rather than months. This shift has disrupted traditional vendor relationships, compressed sales cycles, and increased demand for real‑time analytics and compliance monitoring.

Startups, many of which have built their value propositions around AI‑driven products, find themselves at a crossroads. While they possess the agility to innovate, they lack the established sales networks and long‑term contracts that secure enterprise contracts. Moreover, the new buying criteria—such as data sovereignty, regulatory compliance, and multi‑tenant architecture—require expertise that many early‑stage companies have yet to develop. As a result, a growing number of startups are partnering with larger incumbents or forming strategic alliances to gain credibility and access to enterprise buyers.

Industry analysts predict that the next wave of AI‑focused startups will need to adopt a hybrid approach: maintaining their core innovation while building robust compliance frameworks and scalable deployment models. Companies that can demonstrate clear ROI, secure data handling, and seamless integration with existing enterprise ecosystems will be best positioned to capture the fragmented market created by the AI‑driven shift in buying patterns.
author: TechCrunch

title: Tesla Seeks Cybercab Fleet Buyers
content:
A technology firm announced on Thursday that it has added a new online form to its website to collect contact information from individuals and organizations interested in purchasing Cybercab fleet vehicles. The solicitation, posted on the company’s official site, invites prospective buyers to submit basic details such as name, company affiliation, and intended vehicle quantity, with the aim of facilitating follow‑up discussions about bulk acquisition options.

The Cybercab line, marketed as an electric, autonomous solution for commercial transportation, has been highlighted in recent industry reports as a growing segment of the fleet market. By gathering interested parties through the web form, the company seeks to gauge demand, streamline the sales pipeline, and potentially accelerate the rollout of its vehicles to corporate and municipal fleets. The initiative reflects broader trends toward electrified and automated transport solutions in the logistics sector.
author: TechCrunch

title: Oura Files for IPO Amid Strong Revenue Growth
content:
Ring maker ABC Ringmakers Inc. announced that its business has experienced significant revenue growth over the past year, reporting a 12.4 % increase in total sales compared with the same period in 2023. The company attributed the rise to a combination of higher demand for luxury and engagement rings, as well as a successful expansion of its online retail platform, which now accounts for 38 % of total revenue.

In a statement released on Thursday, ABC Ringmakers highlighted that its gross profit margin improved from 28.7 % to 30.3 % during the year, driven by streamlined supply‑chain operations and a shift toward more cost‑effective sourcing of precious metals. The company also noted that its customer base grew by 9 % in the United States and 15 % internationally, reflecting a broader recovery in the global jewelry market following the pandemic‑related slowdown.

Industry analysts view the company’s performance as a positive sign for the broader luxury goods sector, which has been gradually regaining momentum as consumer confidence rebounds. ABC Ringmakers plans to continue investing in digital marketing and product innovation to sustain its growth trajectory in the coming years.
author: TechCrunch

title: OpenAI launches Astra model, claims new era of AI
content:
San Francisco‑based OpenAI unveiled its latest model, Astra, on Thursday, branding it as “the world’s most intelligent and aligned model.” The announcement came shortly after OpenAI president Greg Brockman declared that humanity has entered a new era of artificial general intelligence (AGI). Brockman’s statement follows a recent comment from OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, who described the term “AGI” as an “irrelevant marketing term” only days earlier.

The release of Astra follows a serious AI safety incident involving other models under development at OpenAI, which prompted international concern and a temporary halt to Astra’s training. Despite the pause, the company proceeded with the launch, emphasizing the model’s alignment and performance improvements. OpenAI has not disclosed specific technical details of Astra, and regulators and industry observers are awaiting further information on how the safety concerns have been addressed.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Meloni's government becomes Italy's longest‑lasting post‑war administration
content:
Giorgia Meloni’s hard‑right coalition marked a historic milestone on Friday, becoming the longest‑lasting government in Italy’s post‑World‑II era. The achievement arrives as the ruling bloc prepares for national elections scheduled for next year, a period that analysts say will test the administration’s durability and policy agenda.

In a France 24 interview, journalist Sharon Gaffney spoke with Nathalie Tocci, director of the Istituto Affari Internazionali and professor of practice at Johns Hopkins SAIS, who attributed Meloni’s longevity to a blend of strategic maneuvering and circumstance, noting it is “50 percent savvy political tactics and 50 percent extraordinarily good luck.” Tocci cautioned that despite the record, the government faces significant challenges ahead, including coalition cohesion and voter sentiment, factors that will shape the forthcoming electoral contest.
author: France 24

title: Nvidia to acquire Hugging Face for $12.93 billion
content:
Nvidia announced on Thursday that it will acquire AI developer platform Hugging Face for $12.93 billion, marking the chipmaker’s latest large‑scale investment aimed at deepening its presence in the open‑source artificial‑intelligence ecosystem. The transaction, which is expected to close later this year pending regulatory approval, will integrate Hugging Face’s widely used models and tools with Nvidia’s hardware and software stack, positioning the company closer to the developers who build and deploy generative‑AI applications.

The acquisition is intended to broaden Nvidia’s customer base as competing technology firms develop alternative chips to lessen reliance on its GPUs. By combining Hugging Face’s community‑driven resources with Nvidia’s processing power, the deal seeks to create a more seamless pipeline from model creation to deployment, potentially accelerating AI innovation across industries. Analysts view the move as a strategic effort to secure a dominant role in the rapidly expanding AI market, while regulators will assess the impact on competition in the sector.
author: France 24

title: Tunisia's top court upholds up to 45-year sentences for opposition figures
content:
Tunisia’s highest judicial body confirmed on Thursday the prison terms handed down to a group of opposition figures, lawyers and businessmen in a high‑profile conspiracy case, with sentences ranging as high as 45 years. The rulings, which stem from a trial that began in 2022 and involved accusations of plotting against the state, were delivered by the Court of Cassation after the defendants were found guilty of charges including treason, sabotage and illicit financing. The convicted include senior members of the Ennahda party, prominent legal professionals and several entrepreneurs linked to the alleged scheme.

Human rights groups and political opponents denounced the decision, arguing that the verdict reinforces President Kais Saied’s increasingly authoritarian governance style. International observers noted the case as part of a broader pattern of legal actions targeting critics of the president since his 2021 power consolidation. The court’s affirmation of the lengthy sentences underscores the government’s hardline stance on dissent, while raising concerns about the future of judicial independence and political pluralism in Tunisia.
author: France 24

title: Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola seeks first win with Bradley Barcola added for Ipswich Town match
content:
Andoni Iraola, appointed as Liverpool’s head coach earlier this season, has yet to record his first victory in charge as the club prepares for an upcoming league fixture against Ipswich Town. Since taking the helm, Iraola’s side has accumulated a series of draws and defeats, leaving the team positioned in the lower half of the table and prompting a focus on tactical adjustments ahead of the match.

In preparation for the Ipswich tie, Liverpool have secured the services of French winger Bradley Barcola, who joins the squad on a short‑term deal. Barcola, previously with Olympique Lyon, is expected to add width and pace to the attacking line‑up, and his registration was completed in time for the game. The club’s official statement confirmed that Barcola will be available for selection, marking his first involvement with the team under Iraola’s management.

The addition of Barcola comes as Liverpool aim to break their winless streak and climb the standings. The upcoming encounter with Ipswich offers an opportunity for Iraola to demonstrate progress and for the new signing to make an immediate impact.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US Vice President JD Vance refuses to give timeline for ending Iran conflict
content:
A senior official from former President Donald Trump’s campaign voiced doubt during a White House briefing on Thursday, questioning the administration’s characterization of the recent escalation in the Middle‑East as a full‑scale war. The official, who declined to be named, said the term “war” was premature given the limited scope of the latest flare‑up, which involved a brief exchange of fire between Israeli forces and Hamas militants in the Gaza Strip. The briefing, led by the National Security Council, reiterated that the United States was monitoring the situation closely and stood ready to support diplomatic efforts to de‑escalate tensions.

The official’s skepticism highlighted ongoing debate within U.S. political circles over how to label and respond to the conflict. While the administration continues to provide humanitarian aid to civilians and maintain open channels with regional partners, it has stopped short of committing additional military assets. Analysts noted that the distinction between a “conflict” and a “war” carries implications for congressional oversight and potential funding. The White House reaffirmed its commitment to a measured response, emphasizing that any further escalation would be evaluated in coordination with allies and Congress.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Scientists warn 2026-27 El Niño could be strongest on record, boosting heat, droughts and floods
content:
Scientists from leading climate research institutions have issued a warning that the El Niño expected to develop during the 2026‑27 boreal winter could become the strongest on record. Forecasts from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) indicate sea‑surface temperature anomalies in the central and eastern Pacific may exceed 2.5 °C above average, surpassing the 1997‑98 and 2015‑16 events that previously held the record.

Model projections suggest that such an extreme El Niño would intensify global heat waves, expand drought conditions across parts of Africa, the Indian subcontinent, and the western United States, and increase the likelihood of severe flooding in South America, Southeast Asia, and the eastern United States. The heightened atmospheric circulation associated with a strong El Niño is expected to raise average global temperatures by roughly 0.2 °C for the year, while precipitation patterns could shift dramatically, stressing water resources and agricultural production in vulnerable regions. Researchers emphasize that the magnitude of these impacts will depend on the interaction between the El Niño event and ongoing anthropogenic climate change.

Authorities and disaster‑risk agencies are urged to incorporate the heightened threat into preparedness plans, enhance early‑warning systems, and allocate resources for communities likely to face extreme weather. Continuous monitoring of oceanic and atmospheric indicators will be critical to refine forecasts as the event unfolds, allowing governments and humanitarian organizations to mitigate the projected heat, drought, and flood risks.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Nepal to use DNA testing to identify flood victims
content:
Kathmandu – Nepal’s authorities have announced that DNA testing will be used to identify victims of the deadly monsoon floods that swept the country in late August, a move aimed at providing closure to families and improving the accuracy of death toll figures. The Ministry of Home Affairs confirmed that the forensic department, in partnership with the National Forensic Science Laboratory and international experts, will collect DNA samples from recovered bodies and from relatives of the missing, with results expected to be processed within weeks.

The decision follows reports that more than 150 people have been confirmed dead and hundreds remain unaccounted for across the flood‑hit districts of Kaski, Gorkha and Sindhupalchok. Officials said the DNA program will complement traditional identification methods such as visual recognition and dental records, and that a secure database will be established to match profiles. As rescue and recovery operations continue, the government urged relatives to submit DNA samples voluntarily, emphasizing that the initiative is part of a broader effort to ensure transparent and humane handling of the disaster’s casualties.
author: Al Jazeera

title: NYC imposes one-year AI ban for grades K‑8 affecting 600,000 students
content:
A nationwide ban announced by the education ministry will remain in effect for one year and is projected to impact approximately 600,000 students across public and private schools. The directive, issued earlier this week, specifies that the restriction will be enforced uniformly throughout the country, with authorities outlining a schedule for implementation and compliance monitoring.

Officials indicated that the measure is intended to address identified concerns within the education system and will be subject to review at the end of the twelve‑month period. The ministry plans to assess the ban’s outcomes and determine whether adjustments or extensions are warranted, signaling a forthcoming evaluation of its impact on the student population.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UK Prime Minister Burnham and France's Macron discuss border security and Europe‑UK ties
content:
London – Newly appointed British Prime Minister Andy Burnham met French President Emmanuel Macron for his first official bilateral discussion on Tuesday, focusing on a range of issues that both governments describe as shared challenges. The two leaders convened at the Élysée Palace shortly after Burnham’s swearing‑in, emphasizing the importance of continued cooperation despite the United Kingdom’s recent departure from the European Union. Topics on the agenda included strengthening trade links, coordinating responses to energy price volatility, and aligning security strategies to counter terrorism and cyber threats.

Both officials underscored the need for joint action on climate resilience and migration management, noting that coordinated policy can mitigate the impact of climate‑related disruptions and irregular migration flows across the Channel. The dialogue concluded with an agreement to establish a regular ministerial forum aimed at deepening UK‑France collaboration on economic recovery, defence procurement, and research initiatives, signaling a constructive start to Burnham’s tenure in international affairs.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US-Venezuela oil deal labeled modern colonialism by critics
content:
Washington’s approval of a multi‑billion‑dollar agreement that allows U.S. firms to purchase crude from Venezuela’s state‑run oil company PDVSA has sparked accusations of “modern‑day colonialism” from opposition leaders, regional analysts and human‑rights groups. The deal, valued at roughly $2.5 billion over the next five years, marks a significant shift after years of U.S. sanctions that limited American involvement in the country’s oil sector, which historically accounts for more than 90 percent of Venezuela’s export earnings.

Critics argue that the arrangement gives U.S. corporations preferential access to Venezuela’s depleted reserves while the Maduro government retains control over pricing and production, effectively reproducing a pattern of external extraction that benefits foreign investors at the expense of local communities. Supporters contend the partnership provides much‑needed hard‑currency inflows for a beleaguered economy and could help stabilize global oil markets. As negotiations continue, the controversy underscores the broader geopolitical tension surrounding Venezuela’s resource management and the legacy of foreign involvement in the nation’s oil industry.
author: Al Jazeera

title: ICE officer charged federally for lying about January shooting of Venezuelan man in Minnesota
content:
A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer has been indicted on federal charges stemming from a shooting that took place in Minnesota in January. Federal prosecutors allege that the officer’s actions violated federal law, prompting a criminal investigation that culminated in the filing of the indictment. The case marks a rare instance of a federal law‑enforcement officer facing federal prosecution for conduct occurring in the course of a domestic incident.

The Department of Justice’s Office of the Attorney General is overseeing the prosecution, and the officer is expected to appear before a federal magistrate in the coming weeks. If convicted, the charges could result in significant penalties, including imprisonment and loss of federal employment. The indictment underscores the federal government’s commitment to hold its agents accountable for alleged violations of the law, and the proceedings will continue to be monitored by both legal experts and the public.
author: BBC World

title: Enric Mas extends Vuelta lead; Jakob Omrzel wins stage 12
content:
On Thursday, the 166.6‑km climb to Calar Alto produced a dramatic finish in Stage 12 of the Vuelta a España. Slovenian rider Jakob Omrzel took the win, while Spanish Movistar rider Enric Mas extended his overall advantage with a late attack that left his rivals behind. Mas burst away from a chasing group that included red‑jersey contenders Primož Roglič and Félix Gall with roughly 13 km remaining, powering to the line 27 seconds clear of Roglič and solidifying his lead in the general classification.

The move proved decisive: Roglič and Gall, who had started the day second and third on the GC, were unable to respond to Mas’s solo effort. Omrzel’s victory marks his first stage win in the Vuelta, and Mas’s performance further cements his position as the race’s favorite as the event heads into its final stages.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England clinch ODI series with six-wicket win over Ireland as Issy Wong takes five wickets
content:
England clinched the one‑day international series against Ireland with a six‑wicket victory at Derby on Thursday, finishing the chase with 27 overs to spare. Opening the bowling in place of the unavailable Lauren Bell, seamer Issy Wong delivered a career‑best performance, claiming five wickets for just 33 runs. Her early breakthrough came when she dismissed Ireland captain Gaby Lewis, uprooting the leg stump, and she continued to dismantle the lower‑middle order as the visitors attempted to accelerate.

Ireland were bowled out for 165, unable to recover from the early setbacks, while England’s batting line‑up chased the target comfortably, reaching the required total with ample time remaining. Wong’s decisive spell secured the series win for England, leaving the final scheduled match as a formality.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Reform UK pledges £80bn cuts to public spending
content:
At the Reform Party’s annual conference, economy spokesman Robert Jenrick declared that the party will position itself as the “party of fiscal responsibility.” Speaking to delegates and media representatives, Jenrick emphasized the group’s commitment to balanced budgets, reduced public borrowing and disciplined government spending as central pillars of its economic platform.

Jenrick outlined specific measures the party intends to pursue, including tightening fiscal rules, conducting regular reviews of departmental expenditures and prioritising investments that deliver measurable returns.
