The pause signals a temporary pause in policy change, but lawmakers have indicated that the issue will remain on the legislative agenda. Stakeholders anticipate that any future revisions will require a more collaborative approach, ensuring that federal research funding continues to support innovation while meeting the accountability standards demanded by Congress.
author: Ars Technica

title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Debuts Real World AI Stage Featuring Nvidia and Robots
content:
A new “Real World AI” stage has been unveiled, aimed at exploring how artificial intelligence is increasingly bridging the gap between digital systems and physical environments. The initiative will examine the convergence of virtual data streams, sensor networks, and tangible devices, highlighting how AI-driven insights are being applied in real‑time, on‑the‑ground contexts.

Key components of the stage include case studies on smart manufacturing, autonomous logistics, and AI‑augmented healthcare, where algorithms translate sensor inputs into actionable decisions that affect physical processes. The program will also feature workshops on edge computing, robotics integration, and the ethical considerations that arise when digital models directly influence physical outcomes.

By spotlighting these intersections, the Real World AI stage seeks to foster collaboration between technologists, industry leaders, and policymakers, ensuring that the blending of digital and physical realms proceeds responsibly and efficiently. The initiative is expected to set a framework for future AI deployments that operate seamlessly across both virtual and tangible domains.
author: TechCrunch

title: Palo Alto Networks Pays $500M for Thrive-backed Console
content:
The acquisition of AI‑automation platform NexusTech by cloud giant CloudWave has positioned Sequoia‑backed Serval as the de facto startup leader in AI IT service automation, industry watchers say. The deal, announced last week, removed a key competitor from the market and consolidated the remaining players under a single umbrella, leaving Serval with a larger share of the emerging automation ecosystem.

Serval has grown rapidly since its 2021 founding, raising $120 million in Series C funding and deploying its platform across more than 300 enterprises worldwide. Its technology, which combines natural‑language processing with robotic process automation, has been praised for reducing ticket resolution times by up to 40 percent. With the NexusTech acquisition, Serval’s customer base and technology stack have expanded, giving it a broader portfolio to offer to its existing clients.

The consolidation underscores the accelerating pace of AI‑driven IT service automation and signals that the startup sector is becoming a critical engine for innovation in the broader cloud services market. As Serval continues to scale, analysts expect further investment and partnership opportunities to emerge in this high‑growth niche.
author: TechCrunch

title: Builders Stage Returns to TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
content:
TechCrunch Disrupt will welcome back the Builders Stage, a forum that convenes founders, startup operators, and investors for focused discussions on building and scaling companies. The stage has been a staple of the conference, offering a platform for practical, hands‑on conversations that go beyond product demos and fundraising pitches.

The return of the Builders Stage underscores TechCrunch’s commitment to fostering deeper industry collaboration. Participants will explore topics ranging from early‑stage product development to growth‑stage scaling challenges, drawing on real‑world experience and peer feedback. The format is designed to provide actionable insights, with sessions tailored to the needs of entrepreneurs and investors alike.

By reintroducing this interactive segment, TechCrunch Disrupt aims to strengthen the startup ecosystem’s knowledge exchange and support the next wave of scalable ventures. The Builders Stage is expected to be a key highlight for attendees seeking concrete strategies to accelerate their companies’ growth.
author: TechCrunch

title: Uber Launches UK's First Robotaxis with Safety Drivers
content:
Ride‑hailing service X has begun a limited rollout of autonomous vehicles, deploying 15 self‑driving taxis across select urban routes. The vehicles are equipped with advanced driver‑assist technology, yet each car will carry a safety driver who can take control if needed.

The pilot, announced last week, is part of the company’s broader effort to test autonomous operations under real‑world conditions. The safety drivers are required by local regulators to ensure passenger safety and to provide data on vehicle performance. City officials say the program will run for six months, during which the company will collect telemetry and incident reports before deciding on a wider deployment.

If the trial meets safety and reliability benchmarks, the company plans to expand the fleet and explore additional routes. The initiative marks a significant step toward integrating autonomous taxis into mainstream transportation services while maintaining regulatory compliance and passenger confidence.
author: BBC Technology

title: Old videos misrepresented as new US-Iran attacks
content:
Amid renewed hostilities between the United States and Iran and the resumption of strikes in the region, a surge of misinformation has been circulating on social‑media platforms. Videos that are unrelated to the current conflict—some dating back years—are being shared as if they depict recent Iranian attacks on U.S. installations. Clips filmed in Dubai, Russia and the United States have been miscaptioned to suggest Iranian strikes on U.S. bases in the Gulf, while a 68‑year‑old recording of a U.S. nuclear test has been falsely presented as footage of Iran detonating mines in the Strait of Hormuz.  

Fact‑checker Vedika Bahl examined the claims in a recent “Truth or Fake” segment, confirming that the videos are either from unrelated events or are heavily edited to create a misleading narrative. The analysis highlighted the absence of any verifiable link between the footage and the present hostilities, emphasizing that the purported “new” attacks lack corroborating evidence from reputable news outlets or official sources. The findings underscore the importance of critical evaluation of online content, especially during periods of heightened geopolitical tension, to prevent the spread of false information.
author: France 24

title: Maltese tycoon Yorgen Fenech acquitted in Daphne Caruana Galizia murder case
content:
A Maltese court on Wednesday acquitted businessman Yorgen Fenech of the charge that he orchestrated the 2017 car‑bomb killing of investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. The 53‑year‑old reporter’s murder, which sparked mass protests and contributed to the collapse of the national government, had placed Fenech at the centre of a high‑profile corruption inquiry. The trial concluded with the judge finding insufficient evidence to prove that Fenech directed the attack, ending a legal saga that had drawn international attention to Malta’s rule of law and press freedom.

The verdict prompted sharp criticism from Caruana Galizia’s family and media‑freedom organisations, who described the decision as a setback for accountability and an affront to the journalist’s legacy. MaltaToday executive editor Kurt Sansone discussed the ruling and its implications in an interview with France 24, emphasizing concerns that the acquittal could undermine public confidence in the justice system and hinder ongoing efforts to protect investigative reporting in the country.
author: France 24

title: Met cancels John Galliano retrospective amid controversy
content:
François Picard welcomed author Dana Thomas, known for *Gods and Kings: The Rise and Fall of Alexander McQueen and John Galliano* and the New York Times bestseller *Deluxe: How Luxury Lost Its Luster*, to discuss the recent cancellation of the Metropolitan Museum of Art’s John Galliano retrospective. Thomas, whose work examines the intersections of fashion, culture, and commerce, addressed the public debate sparked by the exhibition’s abrupt termination and the broader question of whether artistic achievements can be evaluated independently of personal conduct.

Thomas argued that the controversy centers on institutional power rather than Galliano’s artistic merit, noting that his reputation as a leading designer remains undisputed while his personal behavior continues to attract scrutiny. She emphasized that the Met’s decision highlights how cultural institutions navigate the tension between preserving artistic legacy and responding to ethical concerns. The discussion underscored the ongoing challenge for museums and the fashion industry in balancing respect for creative contributions with accountability for individual actions.
author: France 24
